sub_palette: near_eastern (egyptian) lean + east_asian (japonic) substrate (cross-family fusion, Egyptian-leaning)

blend.lean_parent: near_eastern (egyptian: the per/niut river-temples, the hem-netjer priesthood and god-king ideology, the Pa-/Per-/Niut- construct toponyms, dj/tj/kh phonology, -aa/-et endings, VSO grammar, l>r and v>w)
blend.substrate_parent: east_asian (japonic: the open CV-mora islands and shrine-isles, the kami of mountain and sea, the rice-and-silk-and-jade staple words, the torii-shrine and the castle-town)
blend.lean: Near-Eastern-heavy (Egyptian) - a single fused people of the sun-river-isles, where the temple-Nile of the god-king and the shrine-isle of the sun-goddess's line grew into one tongue and one rite: the sun-disc and the rising sun as one. The Egyptian temple/Nile/rule register is the backbone; the Japonic island/shrine/material/staple words are the substrate. Not a ruling elite over a populace - one merged people, one fused language (per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md).

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_05 (Egyptian, Abydosian register) x BASE_08 (Japonic, Yamataian register). FUSION-FIRST (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): a SINGLE fused tongue, one word per concept, derived by principled sound-change from both parents - not a slash-pair dual-register gloss. CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Egyptian (Near-Eastern) base = Civilized, Japonic base = Clanhold, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Raiko is Civilized (feudal). Concept: the river-temple and the shrine-isle as one - the sun-disc of the temple-Nile and the rising sun of the island-arc, the solar pharaoh and the sun-goddess's line grown into a single rite over the river-cities of a sun-blessed island-realm (an Egypto-Japonic fusion; 'Rai-ko', the sun-child realm). Lean = Egyptian (the rule/temple/Nile/kin/land register, the Per-/Niut-/Pa- construct toponyms, the -aa/-et endings, VSO); substrate = Japonic (island, shrine, mountain, sea, rice, silk, jade - the land, material and staple words). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Egyptian register (allowed, catalog 5.3), with the Japonic substrate words fused into Egyptian phonology; DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Egyptian canon-morphs PRIMARY (the abydosian column: Tjuraa, Oranetj, Geandaa, Numenaa, Riaret, Atjernaa), Japonic kami-morphs SECONDARY (the yamataian / family_east_asian.json japonic column, hardened to Egyptian shape), never real Egyptian gods or Shinto kami. All three alignments (per 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are ENGLISH except the kingdom which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Pharaoh' (the Great House / solar god-king) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great island-house lord, the apt Japonic-substrate co-rank); conlang titles in ruler_native/domain_native (Egyptian) for NPC dialogue. CSV phonetic profile 'Soft consonants with breathy vowels'; grammar 'VSO, Honorific root patterns'.

phonology.palette: Near-Eastern (Egyptian) lean - dj, tj, kh, h, sh, q consonants, l>r and v>w, triconsonantal-flavored stems, -aa/-et endings, VSO order, breathy long vowels - taking up an East-Asian (Japonic) substrate: open CV moras, the five vowels a i u e o, the island/shrine/mountain/sea/rice/silk/jade word-stock, rendaku voicing. Per the CSV: soft consonants with breathy vowels (the Japonic CV gentleness audible beneath the Egyptian dj/tj/kh softening and the long -aa/-et opens); grammar is VSO with honorific root patterns (the Egyptian verb-first order over a substrate of Japonic honorific kami-suffixes reshaped to Egyptian -aa/-et closes). Theophoric on the Egyptian canon-morphs (Tjuraa-, Oranetj-) with the Japonic kami-morphs as the shrine register (Terashaa-, Haganetj-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC and CV-aa/-et opens (Egyptian); Japonic CV-mora roots shed or breathe-out their final vowel into an Egyptian -aa/-et/-u close or harden consonant-final; clusters dj/tj/kh; long breathy -aa; Pa-/Per-/Niut-/Ta- construct toponyms over -maa/-shimaa island-and-shrine elements; stress varies (the Egyptian pattern overrides Japonic pitch-accent).

sound_changes: Japonic open CV-moras adapt to Egyptian shape: the final open vowel breathes out into a long -aa/-et or an -u close, or the stem hardens consonant-final, then takes an Egyptian nominal -aa/-et ending (yama>djamaa, shima>shimaa, mori>meraa, umi>wemaa, kawa>khawaa)

Japonic plain consonants soften toward the Egyptian inventory: k>k/kh, t>t/tj, s>sh before high vowels, d>dj, voiced g/b retained; Japonic l would go r but Japonic has no l (the Egyptian l>r and v>w laws bite on Egyptian-source roots: itru, wadj)
Japonic pitch-accent is overridden; word order is Egyptian VSO; the Japonic -no linking particle is kept honorifically but reshaped (X-no-Y > X-na- / -en-)

the Egyptian a/e/i/o/u vowels with long breathy -aa dominate; Japonic e/o admitted in stressed substrate roots; retain Egyptian dj, tj, kh, sh, q and the Japonic open-vowel color of substrate stems; triconsonantal-root coloring imposed on borrowed stems
very short Japonic roots take an Egyptian -aa/-et/-u ending to reach a CV(C)-aa shape (ko>kuraa, no>nuaa/sekhet-substrate, do>djaa, cha>tjaa)
fusion_rules.source_tilt: island/shrine/mountain/sea/coast/material/staple words from Japonic roots (the substrate land and its making - shima, yama, umi, jinja, kome, kinu, hisui, uma), then filtered to Egyptian phonology; kin-line/rule/temple/Nile/land/quality/abstract/war words from Egyptian roots (the lean register - itru, per, niut, sa, aa, djeser, bia, mesha); every chosen root then run through the one Egyptian-shaped sound-law so the split is invisible at the surface

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Japonic island/shrine/material/staple roots + Egyptian rule/kin/temple/Nile/land roots, all run through one Egyptian-shaped sound-law (CV-moras breathed into -aa/-et opens or hardened, dj/tj/kh softening, VSO); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. One word per concept, no slashes.

toponymic_suffixes: -shimaa (isle; from Japonic -shima, breathed to the Egyptian -aa)
morphology.patronymic_form: the Egyptian filiation 'sa-' (son of) and theophoric given names are the lead form; the Japonic substrate keeps a reduced honorific -na- / -en- (from -no-) before the given name; nobility carry no inherited surname (filiation + epithet, or a Per- house-name) in the Egyptian manner. The throne fuses both - a Nesut who also heads an island Per- house with a -na- shrine-lineage.
morphology.compounding_rule: Egyptian construct-chains (Per-[god], Niut-[god], Pa-[noun], Ta-[land]) layered over fused feature-compounds (quality + island/shrine element): the capital Raiko (the sun-realm, rai + ko), Per-Tjuraa (temple of Tjuraa), Niut-aa (the great city), Kem-djamaa (black-mountain isle), Pa-iushimaa (the isle). Quality + feature in the Egyptian manner: aa (great), kem (black), djeser (sacred) lead the compound.

title_ladder.government: feudal (a fused sun-temple-and-isle realm: the Nesut and his iry-pat kin at the crown over the Tenka-isles, the Sepati-nomarchs over the niut river-cities, the great island-houses - the daimyo of the shrine-isles - sworn beneath; the hem-netjer priesthood and the kannushi-shrine-keepers serve the one sun-rite together)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Egyptian ladder, ascending. Hatia (mayor) barony; Wer-khaset (great-one of the frontier-land) march; Sepati/Sepat (nomarch/nome) county; Mer-mesha (army-overseer/general) duchy; Heqa-aa (great ruler) principality; Nesut (king) kingdom; Per-aa (Pharaoh, lit. the Great House) empire over the Per-aat. DISPLAY titles are English except the kingdom which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Pharaoh' (set in 'ruler', its native Egyptian form remaining Nesut) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great island-house lord, the Japonic-substrate co-rank, its native Egyptian form remaining Mer-mesha). NOTE the foreign term 'Pharaoh' sits at the kingdom tier here (the solar god-king of the realm) while the native Per-aa caps the empire; the English 'Emperor' is shown at the empire tier. The Japonic substrate keeps its shugo-governor and kannushi-priest beneath the Egyptian crown; the hem-netjer (god's-servant) and the scribal sesh stand outside the ladder. Rank native-forms use the real Egyptian register (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Sa-Nesut (king's son / crown prince); Iry-pat (hereditary heir)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, except the kingdom which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Pharaoh' (the solar god-king) and the duchy which uses 'Daimyo' (the great island-house lord). The *_native conlang (Egyptian) forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric) + Egyptian filiation (sa-X) and/or earned epithet; no inherited surname; the Japonic-substrate folk add a reduced honorific -na- shrine-lineage before the given name; order given-first (both parents agree - the Egyptian given-first and the reshaped Japonic honorific link).
people_name_convention.dual_register: the temple-and-Nile register carries Egyptian theophoric names (X-hotep, X-mose, Mery-X, Sa-X) on the morphed canon-stems; the island-shrine substrate carries fused given names on the kami-morphs (Terashaa-, Haganetj-) with -masaa/-himet endings breathed to the lean phonology.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Egyptian devotional constructs lead: X-hotep (X-is-content), X-mose (X-is-born), Mery-X (beloved-of-X), Sa-X (son-of-X) - e.g. Tjuraa-hotep, Mery-Riaret; the shrine register builds on the Japonic kami-morphs: Terashaa-mose (Terashaa-is-born), Haganetj-hotep, Mery-Megumaa.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Egyptian canon-morphs PRIMARY (family_near_eastern / abydosian, the egyptian column: Tjuraa, Oranetj, Geandaa, Numenaa, Riaret, Atjernaa), Japonic kami-morphs SECONDARY (family_east_asian.json theonym_sets.japonic, the yamataian column, hardened/breathed to Egyptian shape), never real Egyptian gods or Shinto kami. The fused rite identifies the sun-temple-power and the shrine-kami as one face - the sun-disc and the rising sun as one: the hem-netjer of the per-netjer and the kannushi of the torii keep the same powers. All three alignments; strong solar god-king and funerary cult fused with the household shrine and ancestral kami.
religion.the_one: Atjernaa (Egyptian; Jp shrine-name Takamaa-no-kami) - the hidden distant maker, the High-Heaven One above the myriad powers, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tjuraa (Jp Terashaa) - the sun and right-order, the solar disc and the rising sun
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Geandaa (Jp Iwanaa) - the enduring earth and mountain
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Numenaa (Jp Amatkazaa) - air, sky and scribe-wisdom

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Atjernaa, Tjuraa the just sun, Oranetj of the sworn oath, Riaret the merciful - at the per-netjer and the torii-grove alike, and names the Chaotic powers as the -kin of the great serpent Hefau or the aramitama (the wild spirits), warded; the right-order of the sun-temple and the kami-rite bind together
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the deified dead (the akhu inscribed on the tomb-stele and the senzaa enshrined at the household jinper) and the river-and-isle spirits of the per-netjer and the shrine-isles; the great powers invoked at temple and torii situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - the war-flame and the devouring serpent, the storm-kami and the mountain-oni - and names the Lawful powers, and Atjernaa, as the tyrant-powers to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as the -kin of the great serpent Hefau (Egyptian) or the aramitama (Japonic wild spirits), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhu the City-Burner (Jp Takebaa the War-Flame); Vacidus -> Wakedjet the Devouring Hefau (Jp Utsuraa the Devouring Void); Lusanto -> Lusantj the Hoard-Worm (Jp Koganaa-Orochaa the gold serpent).

clergy_ladder.9: Hem-netjer Aa (great prophet) / Saishaa (high priest of the realm)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Per-netjer (god's-house/temple) or the Jinper (shrine-isle temple) of [power]: 'the Per-netjer of Tjuraa', 'the Jinper of Terashaa', within its pylon-court and torii-grove.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified dead (akhu) and sun-god-kings venerated at tomb-temples ('the justified [name]', maa-kheru), and the great ancestors enshrined as kami at the isle-jinper (the honored dead); 'the kami [name]'.
